::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Finding the volume using cylindrical shells about the x-axis](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1115572/finding-the-volume-using-cylindrical-shells-about-the-x-axis), asked by [Xorty](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/209881/xorty) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-01-22; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> So I have spent about a hour on this problem and figured it was time to ask for some advice. The problem is to find the volume using cylindrical shells by rotating the region bounded 
> by
> $$8y = x^3,\qquad y = 8,\qquad x = 0$$
> about the x-axis.
>
> I changed the one on the far left to $x = 2*y^{1/3}$.
>
> I said the region of the integral went from $0$ to $8$ and that the integrand is
>
> $$2 * \pi * y * (2* y^{1/3})\,dy$$
>
> I figured the height would be $x = 2*y^{1/3}$ and that the radius is just $y$. Any help would be greatly appreciate since I can't find any help for this online. I searched around and found some similar problems but it still doesn't make sense to me. Thanks!
:::

I agree with you.  The volume is
$$\begin{align*}
\int_0^8 2\pi y x\,dy &= \int_0^8 2\pi y \left(2\sqrt[3]{y}\right)\,dy \\
&= 4\pi \int_0^8y^{4/3} \,dy \\
&= 4\pi \left[\frac{3}{7}y^{7/3}\right]^8_0 = \frac{12\pi}{7} \cdot 2^7 = \frac{1536\pi}{7}
\end{align*}$$
